title: A wrong answer returns 200, so record every call and score a sample to catch it
aria: Every model call goes through one wrapper. In the example, Google moves the alias gemini-flash-latest to a preview model, and the grading feature marks a correct answer wrong while the call returns 200 in 1.4 seconds, so latency and error monitoring see nothing. The wrapper writes a call record with the prompt version and the model that answered, stores the redacted prompt and reply of every call for 14 days, and sends a 2% sample to a queue. A pinned checker model scores the sample, a nightly job compares the daily agreement rate with its alert line, and the owner finds that the response model changed. Pinning the model and replaying the stored prompts fixes it.

build.title: A wrong grade looks like a success
build.text: The grading feature asks Gemini through one wrapper, by the alias `gemini-flash-latest`. The reply is fast and returns 200, so latency and error monitoring see nothing.

build.title: The wrapper writes three things per call
build.text: A call record with the prompt version and the model that answered. The redacted prompt and reply, kept 14 days. A 2% sample, sent to a queue.

build.title: A second model scores the sample
build.text: Off the request path, a pinned checker model reads the redacted text and a rubric. Its AGREE or DISAGREE lands in `llm_eval` as 1 or 0, kept for months.

build.title: A nightly job raises the alert
build.text: At 06:00 the job compares the daily agreement rate with its alert line, 0.92. The owner groups the records by prompt version and response model to find the cause.

build.title: Pin the model and replay
build.text: The fix requests the pinned `gemini-2.5-flash`. The 5 stored prompts replay 10 times each, and 50 of 50 runs pass.

route.title: A wrong grade comes back as a success
route.text: On Monday morning Google points `gemini-flash-latest` at a preview model. The grading feature now marks correct answers wrong. Every call is fast, returns 200 and throws nothing.

route.title: The wrapper writes one record per call
route.text: It logs prompt version 14 and the model that answered, `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025`, a real name. It also stores the prompt and reply with names and emails scrubbed, kept 14 days.

route.title: A second model scores a 2% sample
route.text: Calls that finished normally enter a random 2% draw and go on a queue. The pinned checker model reads the redacted text, the verdict and a rubric. It answers DISAGREE, stored as 0.

route.title: The nightly job sees Monday fall below its band
route.text: The alert line 0.92 sits three standard deviations below the 30-day mean. Monday scores 0.81, so the alert fires at 06:00 Tuesday. The first learner reports come that afternoon.

route.title: Grouping by version shows the model moved
route.text: The prompt is version 14 on every call, so no prompt edit caused it. The response model changes on Monday, and answers graded wrong go from 4% to 19%.

route.title: Pin the model and replay ten times
route.text: The team requests `gemini-2.5-flash` instead of the alias. The owner replays each of the 5 stored prompts 10 times. All 50 runs pass, and the barista case joins the test set.
